# Final Review Votes
**Producer:** agent:claude/claude-opus-4-6

## Summary

Reviewed all four amendments against the codebase. Accepted three: doc comments for Monod functions (clear maintainability win), porosity documentation for substrate displacement (real physics modeling gap), and renaming the ambiguous water_volume_l API (genuine API design defect with two incompatible semantics). Rejected the legacy constant linking amendment because the legacy reference volume (20L) already differs from the default geometry gross volume (22L), proving these are independent calibration constants — asserting equality would be immediately wrong.

## Votes

- `fr-8-cd41c2dd`: Accept
  Verified in nitrogen_cycle.rs: monod_rate has only a terse one-line doc comment ('Monod-style rate: vmax * biomass * environmental_factor * S/(K+S)') with no units information, and monod_factor has no doc comment at all. After the concentration migration, these functions receive mg/L values, but the parameter names 'substrate' and 'k_substrate' carry no unit indication. Adding brief doc comments noting that both parameters must share units (mg/L post-migration) is a zero-cost maintainability improvement that prevents a real bug class — passing total-mg values instead of concentrations would silently produce wrong kinetics.
- `fr-8-b5b1b923`: Accept
  Verified in geometry.rs:23-30: substrate_displacement_l computes footprint_area_cm2 × capped_depth_cm / 1000.0 with no porosity adjustment. The entire substrate column is treated as 100% solid. Real aquarium substrates (InertSand, InertGravel, CoarsePorous — all present in SubstrateKind) have 30-40% porosity. SubstrateLayerState already has several material property indices (detritus_trapping_index, low_oxygen_tendency_index, etc.) but no porosity field. This overestimates displacement by 30-40%, underestimates net water volume, and propagates into all concentration calculations via TankState::water_volume_l(). At minimum, a doc comment documenting the 100%-solid assumption is necessary; a porosity field would be the proper physics fix.
- `fr-8-bdd60b5c`: Reject
  Verified that LEGACY_KINETIC_REFERENCE_VOLUME_L = 20.0 L while TankGeometry::default() yields 40cm × 25cm × 22cm / 1000 = 22.0 L gross volume. These already differ by 10%. The legacy constants are fixed calibration reference points for the ProcessParams parameter space, not derived from any particular geometry. A compile-time assertion linking them to TankGeometry::default() would fail immediately for volume (20 ≠ 22). The footprint happens to match (0.1 m²) but this is coincidental — the constants serve different purposes. If anything, a clarifying comment that these are independent reference values would help, but the proposed compile-time assertion would be incorrect.
- `fr-8-91607365`: Accept
  Verified both methods: TankGeometry::water_volume_l() (geometry.rs:19) returns length×width×fill_height/1000 (gross prism volume), while TankState::water_volume_l() (state.rs:177) returns net volume after substrate displacement. Having identically-named public methods with incompatible semantics on closely related types is a genuine API design defect. The ratio helpers surface_area_to_volume_ratio (line 56) and wall_area_to_volume_ratio (line 65) compound the problem by building on gross volume without documentation. Renaming the geometry method to something like gross_volume_l or filled_volume_l would eliminate the ambiguity and make it immediately clear when code uses gross vs net volume. This prevents a real class of wiring bug in concentration calculations.
